summary.headline: Adani Green Q1 FY27 power-supply EBITDA rose 33% YoY to INR4,122 crore (94% margin), with merchant risk shifted to AESL via 15–25 year contracts.
summary.overview: Energy sales grew 30% YoY to 13.7 billion units on 4.3 GW of added capacity, and power-supply revenue rose 29% to INR4,280 crore. Management said it has moved previously merchant capacity (including battery storage) onto long-term contracts with Adani Energy Solutions (AESL) on an arm's-length basis, de-risking AGEL's returns. Battery storage commissioning reached 3.5 GWh at Khavda after 1.9 GWh was added in the quarter, against a target of 10+ GWh in FY27. Curtailment remains a 5–7% EBITDA drag until Khavda transmission is complete, which management expects by end-CY2026.

financial_highlights.change: expected about INR21,000 crore by end FY27
current, expected to fall to nil from Khavda by end CY2026

segments.name: Solar and wind (power supply)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR4,280 crore and EBITDA INR4,122 crore in Q1 with 94% margin; energy capacity addition of 4.3 GW (27% increase) supported volumes.

segments.name: Battery energy storage (BESS)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 3.5 GWh after 1.9 GWh added in Q1 at Khavda; FY27 EBITDA guided at INR25–30 lakh per MWh, with the first 3.5 GWh contract fully capitalised by May end. BESS will be reported separately from next quarter.

segments.name: C&I (sold to AESL)
segments.commentary: Previously merchant capacity, including batteries, now contracted to AESL: solar and wind for 25 years at fixed rates, batteries for 15 years, with indicative solar/wind benchmark of about INR2.7–3.5 per unit (as analyst quoted; not confirmed by management).

guidance_outlook: Add 5 GW of greenfield RE capacity in FY27, excluding BESS and pump storage.
Reach 10+ GWh cumulative BESS capacity in FY27; long-term ambition of about 50 GWh by FY30.
Commission the 500 MW Chitravathi pump storage project (Andhra Pradesh) in FY27.
FY27 capex guidance about INR42,000 crore.
Another 7 GW of evacuation (transmission) capacity expected by end CY2026, with the balance a quarter or two later.
Battery capex thumb rule of about INR1.5 crore per MWh; FY27 BESS EBITDA INR25–30 lakh per MWh.
capex_capacity: Khavda: over 10 GW of solar, wind and hybrid assets already included in the group's capacity.
BESS installed 3.5 GWh (1.6 GWh at end FY26 plus 1.9 GWh in Q1); management says it is about half of India's operational battery capacity and will exceed two-thirds by year-end.
Chitravathi 500 MW pump storage on schedule for FY27; other pump hydro projects about two years away.
PPA coverage: 31% of annual PPA requirement achieved in Q1; management expects roughly 100% annually, with a 2–3 year average CUF of about 109–110%.
Management said 5 GW addition target excludes BESS and pump storage.
demand_pricing: Infirm power realisations about INR2.5 per unit, including RECs, in line with merchant pricing.
BESS arbitrage spread assumed INR4–5 per unit (buy around INR2.5, sell in evening peaks), based on 12–36 month price trends.
AESL contracts follow SECI PPA standards with no termination for convenience; management said pricing is at benchmark rates set by arm's-length process and Audit Committee review.
Management sees rooftop solar growth (cited about 8 GW last year) as not disrupting utility-scale demand, citing evening and night peak needs.

qa_highlights.question: How much does curtailment cost in Q1 and when does it end?
qa_highlights.answer: Curtailment costs 5–7% of EBITDA currently; management expects no curtailment from Khavda by end CY2026 as transmission comes online.

qa_highlights.question: Why were merchant/C&I projects moved to AESL and on what terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is de-risking AGEL for long-term predictable returns; contracts are 25 years for solar/wind and 15 years for batteries, fixed-price, with no change expected over the term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 BESS EBITDA trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided INR25–30 lakh per MWh for FY27, with the full benefit of the first 3.5 GWh contract coming in over the next nine months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR42,000 crore, for roughly 5 GW of RE expansion and 10+ GWh of batteries.

qa_highlights.question: What are battery cost and fire risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR1.5 crore per MWh; management said the recent fire was in PCS/inverter (IGBT failure), not the battery, and that systems are insured under standard policies.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7 GW evacuation capacity on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects another 7 GW by end CY2026, with the remainder within a quarter or two, and monitors evacuation closely to manage capital cost of delays.

risks_watch: Curtailment (5–7% of EBITDA) persists until the transmission for about 7 more GW is commissioned by end CY2026.
Related-party concentration: AESL now contracts the former merchant and C&I output, so AGEL's revenue depends on an arm's-length counterparty.
BESS commissioning is back-ended (10+ GWh in FY27 from 3.5 GWh installed), and management declined quarterly phasing guidance.
Battery fire-risk perception and second-cycle or cycle-count economics remain unproven.
Expansion of the target to 50 GWh by FY30 and the rooftop solar build-out may affect long-term demand.
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution and the Khavda ramp-up, but evasive on specific AESL pricing (declined to disclose per-kWh rates) and on BESS quarterly phasing, citing the early-stage nature of battery projects.
key_quotes: We surpassed 20 GW milestone, making it India's largest and fastest greenfield renewable capacity addition.
We commissioned 1.9 GW of battery energy storage capacity at Khavda during the quarter, taking total installed capacity to 3.5 GW-hour.
In order to de-risk ourself and concentrate more on the project execution and operational excellence, on a long -term basis, we have contracted on an arm's length basis
a curtailment has an impact of in the range of 5% to 7% on our overall EBITDA as we speak.

growth.why: Management reiterated 5 GW greenfield RE addition and 10+ GWh BESS for FY27 with FY27 capex of about INR42,000 crore, and run-rate EBITDA guided from INR17,000 cr to about INR21,000 cr; Q1 revenue +29% and EBITDA +33% YoY, with 1.9 GWh BESS already added and 7 GW evacuation due by end CY2026, though the 5 GW greenfield and 10+ GWh targets lack detailed project-level timing in the brief.
